title: Transverse conformal volume expansion forces topological entropy on a compact foliated manifold
source_title: Invariant submanifolds of conformal symplectic dynamics
author: Marie-Claude Arnaud; Jacques Fejoz
difficulty_reason: Transverse volume growth alone does not give an entropy bound when images of a transversal can return through many plaques. The authors construct a uniform leafwise-distance comparison and a finite product-chart partition, then prove that each dynamical itinerary intersects every terminal plaque at most once. This new geometric control gives a uniform volume bound per itinerary and forces exponentially many itineraries, rather than relying on the smoother Yomdin volume-growth theorem.

Complete authored proof10–13, including leafwise distance Lemma1, product neighborhoods, inverse-map control and induction on dynamical cube intersections, is retained. The presymplectic and conformal-symplectic constant-rank corollaries13 are supporting context only, not separate variants; no noncompact entropy extension is asserted. historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The author constructs uniformly controlled leafwise product neighborhoods and proves that every refined dynamical cube intersects a transversal at most once per local leaf. This controls transverse volume independently of leafwise local entropy and yields a low-regularity entropy lower bound, beyond qualifying-exam dynamical systems.
